name: Semicolon Usage Frequency
description: Analyzes the frequency and grammatical context of semicolon (;) usage. In organic human writing, the semicolon is a notoriously controversial and relatively rare punctuation mark; many writers avoid it entirely, while others use it stylistically. AI models, trained extensively on formal academic texts, high-quality literature, and programming code, understand the precise grammatical rules of the semicolon and tend to use it with rigid, mathematically predictable perfection and at rates that often deviate from average human baselines.
algorithm: Punctuation Distribution Frequency and Contextual Syntax Matching
mechanism: The algorithm counts the absolute frequency of semicolons per 1,000 words and evaluates the syntactic structures connecting the clauses on either side. It measures the 'Semicolon Density' against a baseline calibrated for the specific text genre (e.g., informal blogs vs. academic papers). AI-generated text often exhibits 'hyper-correctness'—using semicolons flawlessly to connect independent clauses where a human might naturally use a period or conjunction out of habit or for stylistic pacing. The system flags texts where semicolon usage is unusually high, perfectly rigid, or misaligned with the text's overall informal register.
useCase: Useful as a hyper-specific heuristic in analyzing student essays, blog posts, and emails where formal punctuation marks feel out of place against the expected human tone.
strengths:
• Highly effective secondary indicator; humans rarely use semicolons perfectly consistently across long documents without formal editing.
• Fast, lightweight, and language-independent (for languages that utilize the semicolon).
limitations:
• Easily bypassed if the AI is specifically prompted not to use semicolons.
• High false-positive rate for professional editors, academics, and novelists who intentionally and correctly utilize complex punctuation.
parameters:
Analysis: Punctuation Frequency and Syntactic Clause Boundaries
Metric: Semicolons per 1,000 words and Register Alignment
Output: 0-100 Punctuation Artificiality (Hyper-correctness) Score
accuracy: Low to Moderate — 50-65% accuracy. Operates strictly as a supportive, micro-level feature within the broader Punctuation Pattern analysis pipeline.

references.title: Manning, C.D. & Schütze, H. (1999). Foundations of Statistical Natural Language Processing. MIT Press.
Uchendu, A. et al. (2020). Authorship Attribution for Neural Text Generation. EMNLP.
